changes: Complete ordered row partitions scatter directly into the existing spare buffer, then swap ownership. Partial/unordered ranges keep the original copy/in-place path.
Stable feature-key radix sorting uses only the bits needed for feature IDs in [0, columns). All-zero high-key passes are omitted; the one-feature case skips the feature sort.
measurement: Two sequential experiments, each 18 fresh workers: three CPU controls, three baseline MPS and three candidate MPS per workload. 100 rounds, eight CPU threads, warmed runtime; loading/setup/final prediction excluded from training and reported separately. This task ran no concurrent builds/tests/other benchmarks; unrelated sessions and applications were not controlled.

cpu_sampling_diagnostic.scope: CPU call stacks after first boosting round; profiling overhead invalidates performance comparisons. Models/margins match the unsampled candidate.
cpu_sampling_diagnostic.sampled_process_physical_footprint: 3.1 GB current / 6.9 GB peak as reported by macOS sample; differs from process RSS
cpu_sampling_diagnostic.interpretation: Most captured main-thread stacks wait for Metal command completion, particularly in split evaluation and prediction. This includes necessary GPU execution and scheduling; the sample does not establish that all wait time can be removed or explain all benchmark variability.

limits: Targeted GPU timings improved; end-to-end training benefit is inconclusive under the observed system conditions. The combined wide-data candidate was slower in all three pairs. HIGGS baseline training ranged from 47.543 to 103.801 seconds; its apparent median speedup must not be generalized.

User applications remained open and system-wide swap was substantial. AC power and clock continuity were checked. These observations do not isolate memory pressure, other CPU/GPU activity or hardware limits.

Kernel stage diagnostics use five randomized alternating measurements per variant and exact CPU references. Partition stages use separate command buffers, unlike production. The feature-key diagnostic excludes value sorting and other sketch work; its speedup is not a training speedup.
GPU counter families may overlap and cannot be summed or subtracted from training wall time to infer CPU overhead.
The CPU-sampled worker is excluded from timing comparisons. Dataset sizes are full, but 100 rounds is not the historical 1000-round HIGGS workload. One Apple GPU was tested.
